text:
### Observed differences

- **A02 disappeared from the execution paths.** In the earlier window A02 ran in about 26 of 100 cases (53 of 200 traces); in the later window it appears in none of the 200 traces. Before, A03, A07, A08 and A13 — each present in roughly 13–27 of 100 cases — occurred exclusively in traces that also contained A02; in the later window each of them occurs only without A02. [OCC002, POS002, REL011, REL014, REL015, REL019]

- **Flow around A02 was rerouted.** Before, about 92 of 100 of A02's outgoing transitions stayed inside the group (A07 about 42, A03 about 26, A08 about 13, A13 about 11), and A03, A07, A08 and A13 each sent a share back to A02 (about 15, 34, 11 and 4 in 100); in the later window none of these transitions is observed. Instead, A03 exits to A05 in about 85 of 100 outgoing transitions (about 65 before), A08 in about 62 (about 30 before), A07 passes directly to A03 (about 48, up from about 21) and to A13 (about 29, up from about 8), and A07/A08 reach A05 about one step sooner than before. The group itself continues at slightly lower shares (A07 about 26→24, A08 and A13 about 13→11 in 100 cases). [DIR002, DIR003, DIR005, DIR006, DIR009, LAG009, LAG010, LAG013, OCC007, OCC008, OCC013]

- **A01 changed placement and successor.** Before, A01 sat late in its traces (mean normalised position about 0.82) and was always immediately followed by A05; in the later window it is the first event of every trace containing it (position 0) and is always immediately followed by A06. [POS001, DIR001]

- **The order between A01 and the A06/A11/A12 group reversed.** Before, A11 and A12 each preceded A01 in all of their roughly 27-in-100 co-occurring traces, and A06 ran before A01 or interleaved with it; in the later window A01 precedes A06, A11 and A12, which now sit later in the trace (mean positions about 0.22→0.35 for A06, 0.55→0.75 for A11, 0.52→0.67 for A12). A11 and A12 now lead to A05 (about 70 and 30 of 100 of their outgoing transitions) one to two steps sooner than before, while the A01→A05 distance grew from always one step to about four steps (observed within five steps in 22 of the 43 later A01 traces). [REL004, REL008, REL009, DIR007, DIR008, LAG001, LAG021, LAG022, POS004, POS008, POS009]

- **Participation shifted moderately.** A01, A06, A11 and A12 each fell from about 27 to about 21–22 of 100 cases, A05 from about 54 to about 46, A10 from about 15 to about 11, and A06's repetitions fell from 0.60 to 0.43 occurrences per trace; A04 (about 23→27) and A09 (about 24→27) rose slightly, though differences of this size are common in random splits. [OCC001, OCC005, OCC006, OCC010, OCC011, OCC012, OCC004, OCC009]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that case flow no longer routes through A02. In the earlier window, A02 ran in about 26 of 100 cases as the hub of a tightly coupled group: it always appeared together with A07 (in either order), and A03, A08 and A13 occurred only alongside it, with about 92 of 100 of A02's outgoing transitions leading back into this group and the rest exiting to A05. In the later window, A02 is not observed in any trace, every transition into it from the still-active A03/A07/A08/A13 has disappeared, and those activities now pass directly among themselves and exit to A05 (A03→A05 up from about 65 to about 85 of outgoing; A08→A05 from about 30 to about 62; A07→A03 now always one step apart where about 45 of 100 such pairs previously had an activity between them). This is shown directly and consistently by participation, successor and co-occurrence indicators, with differences larger than in 199 of 200 random re-splits, and the group itself persists (A07 still in about 24 of 100 cases), which fits the A02 step being dropped from these paths rather than a whole path disappearing. The competing explanation that cannot be ruled out is that A02 still executes but far below its earlier rate — zero participation only means it was not observed in the later sample — although the simultaneous loss of all incoming edges from activities that still run makes a pure sampling dip unlikely; also, no screening baseline was supplied, so the number of qualifying items could not be checked against a formal chance expectation. [OCC002, POS002, DIR002, DIR003, DIR005, DIR006, DIR009, REL011, REL014, REL015, REL019, LAG009, OCC007]

Other differences: A second, separately supported reordering affects the A01 segment, whose traces contain none of the A02-group activities in either window. A01 moved from the end of its traces (always followed directly by A05) to the first event, now feeds into A06, and the A06/A11/A12 block that previously preceded it now follows it, with A11 and A12 exiting to A05 one to two steps sooner; the A01→A05 distance grew from one step to about four. Participation of this group also fell (A01, A06, A11 and A12 from about 27 to about 21–22 of 100 cases; A05 from about 54 to about 46; A10 from about 15 to about 11), and A04 and A09 rose slightly to about 27 of 100, a small shift that random splits commonly produce. This reordering rests on direct order reversals, successor changes and position shifts rather than on inference, but the absence of a screening baseline means the item counts could not be compared with a chance expectation. [POS001, DIR001, REL004, REL008, REL009, DIR007, DIR008, LAG001, LAG021, LAG022, POS004, POS008, POS009, OCC001, OCC005, OCC006, OCC010, OCC011, OCC012, OCC004, OCC009]
